candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Ave
candidates.price_text: day passes from about $29, varies by day and time
candidates.summary: Bathhouse's third New York location opened in 2026 at 540 Atlantic Avenue, in the shadow of Barclays: 32,000 square feet of thermal pools, saunas, steam rooms, cold plunges and an outdoor pool, plus the usual scrub and massage menu and a restaurant. Day passes start around $29 depending on the slot.
candidates.fit: The full-bathhouse-day-with-a-friend thing he rates highest, except this one is a fifteen-minute walk from Fort Greene instead of a trek to Williamsburg or Borough Park. Book an early slot, bring one friend, spend four hours, be home for bedtime.

candidates.title: Rétromobile New York (inaugural US edition)
candidates.time_text: show hours on the ticket page
candidates.summary: The 50-year-old Paris collector car show lands in New York for the first time, November 19 to 22 at the Javits Center, with a Gooding Christie's auction running alongside it and Hagerty, Petersen and a vintage-watch show as partners. Four days, one room, serious metal rather than a dealer expo.
candidates.fit: A once-ever first edition in his own city, and the opposite of a corny cars-and-coffee: an auction floor you can walk, with people who actually own the cars. Book this one now — it is the radar item of the month for the car lane.

candidates.title: Daybreaker Heatwave: Sauna Rave
candidates.summary: Daybreaker's night edition at Othership Williamsburg: guided sauna rounds and ice plunges led by the Othership team, then a DJ set and dancing, sober, 9pm to midnight. A second edition runs the morning of November 29, 9am to noon.
candidates.fit: Flagging it for one reason: Diplo played the October 23 edition of this exact thing at this exact address, unannounced to most people. The format is otherwise filler, but it is the one sauna night in the city where a Tier 1 name can turn up in a 150-person room, so watch the lineup when it posts.

candidates.title: Beat Drop: DJ Takeover
candidates.time_text: evening; start time on the booking page
candidates.summary: A two-hour sauna-and-ice-bath session with a live DJ playing the room rather than a recorded playlist, at Othership's Williamsburg location. Runs roughly every other Saturday; the next Williamsburg edition after this is November 28.
candidates.fit: A Saturday night out that isn't a bar and isn't a 2am set — contrast therapy with a live DJ, two hours, home at a reasonable time. Use it as the recovery version of a night out with one friend rather than the main event.

candidates.title: NYCRUNS Great Gobble 5K
candidates.summary: A 5K around Prospect Park benefiting the YMCA of Greater New York, 9am start on the Saturday before Thanksgiving. Entry through NYCRUNS; price on the race page.
candidates.fit: Twenty-five minutes of work, in his back yard, finished before the day starts — the kind of thing you can talk two friends into on a group text and still be home by 10:30. Register in the next week or two; the Prospect Park ones fill.

candidates.title: F1 2026: Las Vegas Grand Prix, live in the screening room
candidates.summary: The Vegas race starts at 11pm New York time and Classic Car Club shows it live in its clubhouse screening room, with overflow screens in the bar and restaurant. The club notes the drivers' title is already settled — Antonelli — but the constructors' championship is still open. A replay screening runs November 22 at 1pm.
candidates.fit: A late Saturday race in a car club rather than a sports bar, with people who care, and the 1pm Sunday replay if 11pm is too late for a dad. Caveat before you plan it: Classic Car Club's screenings are listed under member events, so call and confirm you can buy in as a guest.

candidates.title: World Spa
candidates.summary: A 50,000 square foot bathhouse in south Brooklyn with eight heat rooms under one roof: the largest Russian Grand Banya in the US with venik (birch and oak branch) treatments, a Moroccan hammam, a Himalayan salt room, a snow room, an event sauna that runs theatrical Aufguss rituals, plus pools and a full restaurant.
candidates.fit: He did the East Village banya with a friend and called it a highlight; this is that day at ten times the scale, with the venik parilka and an event sauna doing Aufguss theater. Six hours, two guys, a long lunch in robes in the middle. Price not confirmed — check the day pass page before you commit.

candidates.title: TWA Hotel rooftop pool day pass
candidates.address: One Idlewild Drive, JFK Airport, Queens
candidates.summary: The heated rooftop pool on top of the Saarinen TWA terminal at JFK, open in winter, overlooking the runways and the taxiing aircraft. Sold as timed day passes; infrared sauna on the same deck.
candidates.fit: He has done this once and loved it, and the winter version is better: 95-degree water, cold air, planes rotating off 31L. Flagged as an anytime fallback rather than a dated pick — the pass calendar and price need checking on the day you want.

candidates.title: Clube do Choro with Regional Samauma (Sunday front room)
candidates.price_text: donation at the door, amount not listed
candidates.summary: Every Sunday at 3pm, Fernanda Silveira leads a Brazilian choro jam in the front room at Barbès with Regional Samauma and rotating guests. It is the open front bar, not the ticketed back room, and it runs in the afternoon.
candidates.fit: A backup family-daytime move if the Saturday show is a bust: acoustic Brazilian music at 3pm, a carrier-sized room, a beer for the adults, and you are home before dinner. Low commitment, nothing about it is a kids' event.

candidates.title: Red Baraat at Barbès
candidates.price_text: door charge collected at the door, amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Red Baraat, the Brooklyn dhol-and-brass band that plays Celebrate Brooklyn-sized stages and whose Tiny Desk is one of the most watched ever, is playing the back room at Barbès at 10pm on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Capacity there is a few dozen people. Barbès does not publish a price on the calendar; pay at the door or in advance online.
candidates.fit: This is the pick he says the email keeps missing: a band he could name, in a room far too small for them, ten minutes from Prospect Heights. Horn-driven bhangra-funk that actually makes people dance sits right next to his Afrobeats and dancehall phase, and it is a Friday night with the guys, not a 2am set.

candidates.title: Michael Hearst: The Unusual, Extraordinary, Curious, and Unconventional Songbook
candidates.price_text: door charge or suggested donation, amount not listed
candidates.summary: Michael Hearst (One Ring Zero, Songs for Unusual Creatures) plays his family show at Barbès on Saturday afternoon: a musical and visual run through bizarre animals, odd characters and vehicles you never knew existed, drawn from his books, albums and PBS series. It is in the same small bar room Barbès uses at night, so it is loud enough for a toddler and short enough to survive one.
candidates.fit: A kids' concert in a real music room rather than a playground, which is exactly the family register he asked for, and it is a fifteen-minute drive from Fort Greene. Hearst is weird enough that the adults are not just serving time.

candidates.title: Living Language: Fela Kuti's Afrobeat, played by Antibalas players
candidates.price_text: door charge collected at the door, amount not listed
candidates.summary: Living Language, led by Nikhil P. Yerawadekar with musicians from Antibalas, Akoya Afrobeat and Midnight Magic, plays Fela Kuti's Afrobeat idea in a jazz format at Barbès at 10pm on Friday November 13. Small back room, door charge in person.
candidates.fit: His Afrobeats phase, played live by the people who actually hold up that scene in Brooklyn, in a sixty-person room. A Friday night with one or two friends where you can hear each other between songs.

candidates.title: Maya Lin on Art, Nature, and Memory
candidates.time_text: evening; start time not confirmed on the listing I could read
candidates.summary: Asia Society New York has Maya Lin, the architect of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, in conversation about art, nature and memory on Thursday November 12. It is in Asia Society's own auditorium on Park Avenue, a few hundred seats, with tickets through their site.
candidates.fit: He ticked Asia Society evenings, and this is the version of that with a name he actually knows rather than a panel of fellows. Thursday is his night and it is a clean date-night length with his wife.

candidates.title: Ruth Rehmann's Illusions: Rob Madole and Megan Nolan in conversation
candidates.summary: A reading and panel at the Goethe-Institut around Ruth Rehmann's postwar German novel Illusions, with its translator Rob Madole and the novelist Megan Nolan. Thursday November 19, 6:30 to 8pm, at the Institut's own space; Goethe does not list a price on the event page, and their talks are usually free with RSVP.
candidates.fit: German literature in a room of maybe eighty people, with a contemporary novelist he might actually have read in the chair, on a Thursday. It is the German-culture lane without a Biergarten in sight, and it is the opposite of an arena.

candidates.title: Jung Chang: My Life After China
candidates.summary: Asia Society's Center on U.S.-China Relations hosts Jung Chang, the author of Wild Swans, in conversation with Jiayang Fan on Friday November 20, 6:30 to 8pm, at 725 Park Avenue.
candidates.fit: He ticked Asia Society and the serious foreign-policy lane; this is the China conversation with an author whose book he has probably seen on every shelf, not a think-tank panel of three deputy directors. Friday evening, over by 8.

candidates.title: Germany and the Nuclear Question: Energy Security After the Phase-Out
candidates.venue: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy (webinar)
candidates.summary: Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy runs a lunchtime webinar on Germany's firm-power problem after the nuclear phase-out: how the country keeps dispatchable, affordable electricity and what it means for industrial competitiveness. Tuesday November 10, 1 to 2pm, online, free with registration.
candidates.fit: Two of his lanes in one hour: Columbia's energy centre, which he ticked, and Germany. It is a desk-and-headphones thing rather than a night out, so treat it as background, not a plan.

candidates.title: Storage Is the New Grid: Jobs, Investment, and Community
candidates.venue: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy
candidates.summary: An evening CGEP event, 6 to 9pm on Tuesday November 10, on battery storage becoming core grid infrastructure: investment, jobs and siting. The listing on CGEP's events page gives the date and the three-hour evening slot; I could not open the event page itself to confirm the room, the speaker list or whether it is open to non-Columbia registrants.
candidates.fit: Energy markets and infrastructure is the ideas lane he actually ticked, and a three-hour evening slot usually means a panel plus a reception where you talk to people. It is a Tuesday, so only worth it if the speaker list, once you open the page, is serious.

candidates.title: Annie Proulx: New and Collected Stories
candidates.summary: 92NY's reading series has Annie Proulx, the Pulitzer and National Book Award winner who wrote Brokeback Mountain, launching her New and Collected Stories in conversation on Tuesday November 10. 92NY's readings happen in the Kaufmann Concert Hall or the smaller Buttenwieser Hall.
candidates.fit: He ticked 92NY-style institutions, and this is a writer whose name carries outside book circles doing one night in town. It is a Tuesday, so it only clears his bar as a book-now, one-off, not a regular move.

candidates.title: Hannah Arendt's New York City (self-guided audio walk)
candidates.summary: The Goethe-Institut runs a free self-guided audio walk through the New York of Hannah Arendt, listed as ongoing through the end of 2026. You download it and walk it yourself, at whatever pace you want.
candidates.fit: German intellectual history you can do pushing a stroller on a Saturday morning, free, with no booking. Filed under things to have in your back pocket rather than a plan for this week.

candidates.title: CityKinder St. Martin's Lantern Walk in Prospect Park
candidates.time_text: late afternoon at dusk; the 2026 date and time were not posted on the page I could read
candidates.venue: Prospect Park (near the bandshell, Prospect Park West and 9th Street)
candidates.address: Prospect Park West and 9th Street, Brooklyn
candidates.price_text: $10 suggested minimum donation per child; lanterns and sticks sold at the event
candidates.summary: CityKinder, the German-speaking family network in New York, gathers the German community at dusk every November near the Prospect Park bandshell for a Laternenlauf: lantern songs, a procession through the park, and a re-enactment of St. Martin on horseback sharing his cloak. It is run as a charity fundraiser with a $10 suggested donation per child, and lanterns are sold on site.
candidates.fit: This is the Laternenfest he ticked, in his own park, with the German kids' songs he already plays for the one-year-old. One warning: the organizer page is evergreen and does not carry the 2026 date, so check CityKinder's events page or their Eventbrite before you plan around it.

candidates.title: Jerusalem Baroque Orchestra presents Kedusha
candidates.summary: Israel's Jerusalem Baroque Orchestra plays Kedusha in the Jewish Museum's Scheuer Auditorium, a one-night program of 17th and 18th century music from Jewish communities in Europe. Thursday Nov 12, 7pm to 8:30pm; tickets through the museum.
candidates.fit: The Jewish-culture lane he ticked, in a 250-seat auditorium rather than a concert hall, on his main weeknight slot — a date night that isn't another cocktail bar. I could not read the ticket price, so check before you promise.

candidates.title: Favorite Record: make and trade mixtapes
candidates.summary: New York Emos and grrrrl afraid host a night where you submit a playlist, they burn it to an actual CD, and you decorate the sleeve with supplies on hand, then trade with strangers. Emo and pop-punk on the aux, full bar, 6 to 9pm Thursday. Free with a $5 suggested donation; RSVP and playlist submission through the organizers' link.
candidates.fit: Interactive, early enough for a dad on a Thursday, and squarely in his 2000s pop-punk lane — blink-182 and Jimmy Eat World territory with something to actually do. Yes, it's at All Night Skate again, but the format is nothing like the drag night he was sent.

candidates.title: Go Fact Yourself LIVE with Dean Norris and Kate Micucci
candidates.summary: A live taping of the NPR-affiliated pop-culture quiz show hosted by J. Keith van Straaten and Helen Hong, with Breaking Bad's Dean Norris and Kate Micucci as the guests being quizzed on their self-declared areas of expertise, plus surprise expert guests. Sunday afternoon show at littlefield, 1pm doors.
candidates.fit: Hank Schrader in a 200-cap Gowanus room on a Sunday afternoon is the 'name you know in a room you don't expect' pick he keeps asking for, and it's a live podcast taping, which he ticked. Weekend daytime, home before the kid's dinner.

candidates.title: Puss N Boots featuring Norah Jones
candidates.summary: Norah Jones' country-leaning trio with Sasha Dobson and Catherine Popper plays Brooklyn Bowl on December 9. Brooklyn Bowl announced it on their own feed; tickets through the venue.
candidates.fit: A nine-time Grammy winner playing a bowling alley in Williamsburg — the Fred Armisen-at-the-Bell-House shape of pick the email keeps missing. It's a Wednesday, so it's a book-now radar item, not a this-week plan.

candidates.title: Maccabee Bar NYC, the Hanukkah pop-up, returns
candidates.venue: Saint Tuesday at Walker Hotel Tribeca
candidates.summary: Naomi Levy's Hanukkah-themed cocktail pop-up takes over the Saint Tuesday speakeasy inside the Walker Hotel starting December 1 and runs through New Year's Eve. Reservations released on a rolling 30-day basis and are live now; walk-ins accepted.
candidates.fit: He already loved the Hanukkah bar once, and this is the same operation in a hidden hotel speakeasy — Jewish-culture lane plus the serious-cocktail-bar lane in one. Book the date the moment it opens on the rolling calendar.

candidates.title: Fort Greene Park Tree Lighting, 12th annual
candidates.address: Myrtle Avenue and St Edwards Street entrance
candidates.summary: The Fort Greene Park Conservancy and Myrtle Avenue Brooklyn Partnership light the park tree at the Myrtle and St Edwards entrance, 5 to 6pm, free. Twelfth year.
candidates.fit: His own annual tradition, in his own park, with the kid and whoever else he drags along. One caveat: the Conservancy's listing date reads Friday December 4 while the page blurb still says December 5, so confirm before you print a day.

candidates.title: BRIC's Winter Wonderland
candidates.summary: BRIC House hosts a free day of art, live music, dance and seasonal art-making for all ages on December 5, with a warm drink and performances; full lineup still to be announced. RSVP free through BRIC.
candidates.fit: Second BRIC pick for a reason: free, indoors, ten minutes from his door, and interesting enough for the adults — the register of family outing he actually wants. Day after the tree lighting, so it makes a proper Fort Greene weekend.

candidates.title: The Nutcracker, New York City Ballet
candidates.summary: Balanchine's Nutcracker opens Friday November 27 and runs through January 2 at the Koch Theater. NYCB is pushing ticket sales now and the good dates go first.
candidates.fit: He calls this one of the best things he has done in the city, and it is the one booking that genuinely has to happen in November. Pick a date with the wife now; a weekend matinee also works with a sitter-free afternoon later in the run.

candidates.title: STAMPED: Aya and Friends
candidates.summary: Elsewhere's November calendar lists STAMPED: Aya and Friends on Friday November 27, billed as afrobeats and amapiano. Tickets through Elsewhere; members get free entry.
candidates.fit: The Afrobeats and amapiano phase he is in right now, on the Friday of Thanksgiving weekend when everyone is off and nobody has a plan. Elsewhere has only carried one pick for him so far, so it is not a repeat room.

candidates.title: The Pop Ups with Princess Backpack and Benjamin
candidates.summary: The Jewish Museum's November calendar lists a Sunday November 22 family concert with The Pop Ups, the Grammy-nominated kids' band, plus Princess Backpack and Benjamin. Time and price are on the museum's program calendar.
candidates.fit: A real kids' band in a real museum auditorium rather than a library basement, and it sits in the Jewish-culture family lane he ticked with the Jewish Children's Museum. Confirm the start time on the museum calendar.

candidates.title: Illusions: Rob Madole and Megan Nolan on Ruth Rehmann
candidates.summary: Translator Rob Madole and novelist Megan Nolan discuss Ruth Rehmann's 1950s West German novel Illusions, newly back in print from Faber Editions. Thursday November 19, 6:30pm at the Goethe-Institut, free with registration, books for sale and signing after.
candidates.fit: German culture in a small room on a Thursday, free, and over by eight — the Goethe programming he keeps saying he wants more of, in the back-room-conversation format rather than a lecture hall.

candidates.title: Ayad Akhtar and Daniel Kehlmann on AI and authorship
candidates.summary: The Goethe-Institut and PEN America host Pulitzer winner Ayad Akhtar and German novelist Daniel Kehlmann in conversation about what AI does to authorship and autonomy, Tuesday December 1 at 7pm, $10, with a reception afterward.
candidates.fit: Two writers of real stature, one of them the biggest German novelist of his generation, in a 150-seat institute room for ten bucks. It's a Tuesday, so it only makes the radar — but it's the serious-ideas lane he ticked without being a think-tank panel.

candidates.title: Tristan and Yseult
candidates.summary: Emma Rice's raucous Kneehigh-style staging of the Tristan and Yseult legend, told by the anorak-wearing Club of the Unloved, is back at St. Ann's for the first time since 2014 and runs through November 22.
candidates.fit: European company theater with live band energy and audience-facing clowning, fifteen minutes from his door — the same register as the Schaubühne-at-BAM tick, and a date night that is not a dinner reservation.

candidates.title: Master of the Flying Guillotine, 4K restoration at midnite
candidates.summary: Severin Films' new 4K restoration of the 1976 kung fu classic Master of the Flying Guillotine screens at midnight on Friday November 13 in Nitehawk's Williamsburg midnite series, with food and drink service at the seat.
candidates.fit: He ticked Nitehawk themed screenings and he trains in Williamsburg; a martial-arts cult film at midnight with one or two of the guys is a better late night than a club. Occasional 2am thing, not weekly.

candidates.title: 240 Months of Riotvan: the Leipzig label turns 20
candidates.summary: Leipzig label Riotvan celebrates twenty years in Good Room's main room with Peter Invasion, Panthera Krause and Timo Lee, while Mike Simonetti plays the Bad Room all night. Advance tickets on Resident Advisor.
candidates.fit: An east German label anniversary rather than another touring headliner — the Berlin and Leipzig club register he ticked, in a 300-cap room. If he isn't in the mood for German house this is skippable; the names are not ones he'd recognize.

candidates.title: Friendsgiving tables at Threes Brewing
candidates.price_text: no deposit, pay as you go
candidates.summary: Threes normally doesn't take reservations, but all November, Monday through Thursday, groups up to ten can lock in a table at Gowanus or Greenpoint with drink specials (ginger margarita and black lager pitchers) and the full Grand Army food menu, platters pre-orderable. Book by emailing events@threesbrewing.com.
candidates.fit: The one month of the year he can actually reserve a big table at a brewery he likes, which solves the Thursday group dinner before anyone else thinks of it. Brewery events are on his keep-it-coming list.

candidates.title: Cold Plunge Comedy with Kurt Braunohler
candidates.summary: The Cold Plunge Comedy series announced its December lineup: Kurt Braunohler hosts Hari Kondabolu, Tina Friml, Josh Gondelman and Andrew Fisher in Union Hall's basement on December 2. Tickets through the series' link.
candidates.fit: A recurring basement stand-up show with a name nobody put on a venue calendar for him, and the title alone is in his sauna-and-plunge wheelhouse. I could not confirm whether the cold plunge is literal or a bit, and it's a Wednesday, so treat it as radar.

candidates.title: The State of Things, Wim Wenders on screen with a signing
candidates.summary: Wenders' 1982 film about a stranded film crew screens at Metrograph on Saturday November 14, introduced by cartoonist Nathan Gelgud and critic A.S. Hamrah, followed by a signing of Gelgud's new Reel Politik collection.
candidates.fit: German cinema in a 175-seat room with a conversation attached, rather than a festival. A quieter Saturday option if the Brujeria party is too late a night.

candidates.title: Honky Tonk Happy Hour at Mable's Smokehouse
candidates.summary: Mable's launched a new Honky Tonk Happy Hour with burnt-end tacos, Frito pie and smoked meat samplers, mini margaritas and spiked cherry limeades, with Nashville DJ Taste.air spinning Willie, Waylon and Merle on vinyl, 4 to 8pm. The launch party ran November 5; the recurring night is new.
candidates.fit: Barbecue, country records on vinyl and cheap margaritas in Williamsburg after he trains — the country lane and the hole-in-the-wall lane at once. The recurring day of week is not confirmed anywhere, so call the restaurant before you send the crew.

candidates.title: Strong Rope Brewery 2027 Mug Club
candidates.summary: Strong Rope opened 2027 Mug Club sign-ups through December 1: a free first pour every day you visit, plus member-only brew days, beer releases and parties through the year, and taproom discounts.
candidates.fit: He already spends sunny days in the Red Hook yard; this turns it into an excuse with invitations attached, and the member brew days are the kind of small scene thing he likes. Deadline is December 1, so it's a now-or-wait-a-year decision.

The Tyla second night (Nov 29) and the Sultan Room afrobeats date both need one confirming click.

Gaps this lane still has, all of them because pages would not load or budget ran out: Caveat (site is JavaScript-only and returns an empty shell to the fetcher, same failure as last week), the Tiny Cupboard, Nitehawk, Alamo Drafthouse Brooklyn, Brooklyn Comedy Collective, Brooklyn Art Haus, the Slipper Room, Littlefield (deliberately skipped — five picks in four issues already), Theatre for a New Audience, Irondale, JACK, Roulette, Pioneer Works, Mark Morris, Kings Theatre, Japan Society, Carnegie Hall and current Bushwick gallery openings.
